name: Hair growth shampoo with DHT blockers
lead: Shampoos marketed as DHT blockers are used on the scalp by people who want to keep or thicken their hair as it thins with androgenetic alopecia. The goal is a fuller head of hair and a stronger hairline. The usual active ingredients are ketoconazole, an antifungal also sold as dandruff shampoo, and saw palmetto, a botanical extract; DHT is the androgen that shrinks susceptible scalp follicles.[1][2][3]

Wikipedia's account of hair loss management says follicular 5-alpha-reductase enzymes (types 1 and 2) in the hair papilla convert testosterone to DHT, which stimulates signals such as TGF-beta and IL-6 that lead to follicle miniaturisation in the scalp [3]. Ketoconazole shampoo has been used off-label alongside oral 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, with limited clinical evidence that it may reduce hair loss in some cases, and the same article reports that finasteride, minoxidil and ketoconazole together work better than any one alone [1][3]. Some shampoos and ointments also make existing hair look thicker without changing the growth cycle, a cosmetic effect rather than regrowth [3].
On forums, DHT-blocker shampoo is usually discussed as a low-cost adjunct to finasteride or minoxidil, and users also post about side effects such as scalp dryness and irritation.[4][5]

Ketoconazole itself was discovered by Janssen in 1976 and came into US use in 1981 under the brand Nizoral, which many users still name when they discuss anti-DHT shampoo [1]. Marketing for this product category varies: some products are medicated antifungal shampoos, while others are cosmetic shampoos built around botanicals such as saw palmetto.

paras: Topical ketoconazole is an antifungal used for dandruff and seborrheic dermatitis, possibly by reducing levels of Malassezia yeast on the skin [1]. As an antifungal it inhibits fungal ergosterol synthesis; antiandrogen effects are described as coming mainly from high oral doses that inhibit androgen synthesis, with direct androgen receptor antagonism considered weak [1]. For androgenetic alopecia, the proposed rationale for the shampoo is reduced follicular inflammation. In one study a 2 percent ketoconazole solution produced regrowth in women comparable to 2 percent minoxidil, with slower onset [1]. Wikipedia's hair loss article says ketoconazole may help in women and cites a 1998 long-term study of ketoconazole shampoo in androgenetic alopecia and a 2020 systematic review of topical ketoconazole [3]. Topical forms have not been associated with the liver and adrenal problems seen with oral tablets; redness is a listed side effect [1].

Saw palmetto extract has been studied for benign prostatic hyperplasia, where reviews are mixed: a 2016 review found a standardized extract may relieve urinary symptoms, while a 2023 review of 27 studies reported little to no benefit.[2] For hair, a 2020 systematic review listed topical saw palmetto among agents that helped prevent hair loss, and oral saw palmetto has one small trial showing tentative benefit in mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia, described as limited evidence.[3]

Type 1 and 2 5-alpha-reductase in hair follicles convert testosterone to DHT. At the scalp, androgens stimulate signals such as TGF-beta and dickkopf1 that shrink follicles [3]. The prescription 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors finasteride and dutasteride are described as working better to prevent further loss than to regrow hair; finasteride gave about 30 percent improvement at six months in the cited summary, and its side effects include gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction and depression [3]. Shampoos are applied to the scalp surface and rinsed off, and no published study of finished DHT-blocker shampoos measuring scalp DHT was found.

Users describe lathering the shampoo into the scalp a few times a week and leaving it on briefly before rinsing, often as one step in a hair-loss routine that also includes oral finasteride or topical minoxidil. Wikipedia describes minoxidil as the only topical product FDA-approved for androgenic hair loss in the US, with about 40 percent of men regrowing hair after 3 to 6 months of topical use, which is why shampoo is usually positioned as an add-on rather than a stand-alone treatment [3]. Wikipedia also notes that low-level laser therapy or microneedling combined with finasteride or minoxidil showed substantive increases in hair count [3].

T Nation members have recommended DHT-blocker shampoos or the actual drugs to a man worried about balding, saying they had seen them work well [4]. In a thread on elevated DHT, a poster who described Nizoral as a DHT blocker applied it to oily areas of facial skin to test its effect on shine [5]. In another thread about stopping testosterone therapy to reverse hair loss, a poster wrote that DHT-blocker shampoos can cause sexual dysfunction [7]. A looksmax.org user reported dry, irritated skin after washing with ketoconazole shampoo twice a week for about three months, and a reply asked whether it was working, to which the original poster answered yes [6].
No studies found of finished DHT-blocker shampoos as a product category. Ingredient-level evidence is limited to the ketoconazole and saw palmetto findings above [1][3].

Ketoconazole data include a study in which a 2 percent solution produced regrowth in women comparable to 2 percent minoxidil [1], a long-term shampoo study cited by Wikipedia [3] and a systematic review of topical ketoconazole [3]. For saw palmetto, a single small trial of an oral extract showed tentative benefit in mild to moderate androgenetic alopecia, while a 2020 systematic review listed topical saw palmetto among agents that helped prevent hair loss [3]. Prostate studies of saw palmetto are mixed [2].

lore.intro: DHT-blocker shampoo appears in hair-loss threads on T Nation and looksmax.org as a topical add-on or an alternative to drugs.[4][5][6]

claims.claim: DHT-blocker shampoos can slow or reverse balding
claims.believers: A T Nation poster said they had seen DHT-blocking measures work very well, with some completely reversing balding.[4]
claims.experts: Research on ketoconazole shampoo is limited and mostly concerns women or combination use, and no studies of finished DHT-blocker shampoos as a category were found.[1][3]

claims.claim: Ketoconazole shampoo works as a DHT blocker
claims.believers: Users describe Nizoral, which contains ketoconazole, as a DHT blocker and apply it to the skin.[5]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes the proposed rationale as reduced follicular inflammation and notes limited clinical evidence for hair loss.[1][3]

claims.claim: DHT-blocker shampoos cause sexual side effects like finasteride
claims.believers: A T Nation poster wrote that all of the DHT-blocker shampoos can definitely cause sexual dysfunction and said they avoid the standard ones [7].
claims.experts: Wikipedia lists gynecomastia, erectile dysfunction and depression as side effects of oral finasteride, and says topical ketoconazole has not been linked to the liver and adrenal problems seen with tablets; no study of sexual side effects from DHT-blocker shampoos was found [1][3].

claims.claim: Using a DHT shampoo alongside finasteride or minoxidil boosts results
claims.believers: Forum users commonly describe shampoo as an inexpensive extra step in a routine with drug treatments [4].
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports that finasteride, minoxidil and ketoconazole used together are more effective than any one alone [3].

card.summary: Shampoos with ketoconazole or saw palmetto sold for hair loss, with limited ingredient-level evidence.
card.note: Evidence mostly concerns ketoconazole; saw palmetto hair data were not found.

quick.overview:
These shampoos add ingredients like ketoconazole or saw palmetto and are sold to counter hair loss.
Evidence is limited: ketoconazole has some supportive findings, while saw palmetto's evidence concerns the prostate.
quick.mechanism: Ketoconazole is an antifungal thought to lower scalp inflammation. Saw palmetto is claimed to reduce DHT, but this is not established.
quick.risks: Topical ketoconazole is listed with redness; serious effects relate to oral forms.

chain: Ketoconazole or saw palmetto applied to the scalp
Proposed reduction of follicular inflammation or local DHT effects
Hair loss slows and hair looks fuller
angle.text: People wash with these shampoos to protect or thicken hair on a thinning scalp. Ketoconazole is the better studied ingredient, and the shampoos are often paired with drug treatments.
